title: Severe Cyclonic Circulation & Monsoonal Heavy Rainfall Override
advisory_lead: IMD/Active Low-Pressure Weather Alert: An active low-pressure / severe monsoonal weather system is bringing intense precipitation and turbulent squally winds to the region.
guidance: Treat all outdoor activities as high severity risk regardless of category. Strongly advise postponing non-essential outdoor travel and open-air activities until the convective rain system clears.
precautions: Avoid all outdoor cycling, two-wheeler travel, and open-field activities
Watch for urban waterlogging, localized flooding, and squally gusts
Monitor official India Meteorological Department (IMD) / local disaster authority bulletins

title: Pediatric UV & Thermal Regulation Safety Policy
guidance: Children possess higher body surface-area-to-mass ratios and immature thermoregulatory mechanisms, making them exceptionally vulnerable to rapid dehydration and playground metal equipment contact burns.
precautions: Restrict playground activities to covered or fully shaded facilities
Test metal and dark plastic playground slide surfaces by hand before allowing children contact
Enforce broad-brimmed sun hats and mandatory 15-minute fluid intervals

title: Extreme UV Radiation Advisory for Midday Outdoor Exercise
guidance: High risk of acute cellular UV radiation damage and photo-keratitis during midday hours. Advise strictly against unprotected vigorous outdoor training between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM. Recommend rescheduling high-intensity workouts to early morning (before 9:00 AM) or post-sunset.
precautions: Apply broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen every 2 hours
Wear UV-rated polarized sunglasses and protective breathable apparel
Hydrate with electrolyte-balanced fluids before and during movement

title: Squally Wind & Crosswind Hazard for Cyclists and Two-Wheelers
guidance: Wind speeds exceeding 40 km/h present direct mechanical stability hazards for cyclists and two-wheeler operators due to sudden crosswind gusts, lateral vehicle displacement, and falling debris. Flag as a significant safety risk rather than a mere comfort issue.
precautions: Avoid elevated overpasses, coastal highways, and open corridors prone to wind tunneling
Reduce riding speed by at least 30-50% if transit is unavoidable
Consider shifting to enclosed four-wheeler transit or metro

title: Sub-Freezing & Frostbite Risk for Outdoor Exposure
guidance: Sub-zero temperatures with wind chill dramatically accelerate peripheral hypothermia and frostbite on exposed extremities within 30 minutes of stationary exposure.
precautions: Dress in modular three-layer thermal insulation with windproof outer shell
Keep extremities (fingers, toes, ears, nose) insulated with moisture-wicking wool or synthetic fiber
Consume warm, calorie-dense sustenance and warm fluids regularly

title: Dense Fog & Severe Visibility Reduction for Highway Travel
guidance: Atmospheric conditions favor dense radiative or advection fog causing acute optical attenuation. Advise postponing non-urgent highway transit until atmospheric mixing improves visibility.
precautions: Operate vehicles exclusively with low-beam headlights and dedicated fog lamps; do not use high-beams
Utilize lane guide markings on the roadway shoulder rather than center lines
Avoid sudden braking and maintain dual-hazard flashers if pulling onto the shoulder

title: Heat Stress & Exertional Heat Exhaustion Warning
guidance: Severe heat index condition where evaporative cooling through perspiration is severely impaired, elevating the risk of exertional heat exhaustion and heat stroke. Strongly discourage continuous outdoor endurance cardio.
precautions: Limit continuous outdoor exertion to under 20 minutes with mandatory shade breaks
Pre-cool body and maintain continuous cold fluid intake
Watch for warning signs: dizziness, nausea, cessation of sweating, or muscle cramps

title: Senior & Cardiovascular Thermal Stress Protocol
guidance: Extreme ambient thermal fluctuations impose excessive cardiac workload and vascular constriction or dehydration in elderly individuals and those with cardiovascular vulnerabilities.
precautions: Confine routine walks to temperature-controlled indoor tracks or climate-buffered hours
Carry prescribed emergency medications and a companion communication device
Monitor for orthostatic hypotension or shortness of breath

title: Canine Pavement Hyperthermia & Paw Pad Safety
guidance: Asphalt and concrete surface temperatures can exceed ambient air temperature by 15°C-25°C under direct solar radiation, causing immediate second-degree paw pad burns and canine heat exhaustion.
precautions: Perform the 7-second back-of-hand test on asphalt before walking dogs
Restrict walks to grassy parks, shaded dirt trails, or early dawn hours
Carry portable pet hydration and avoid muzzling that restricts panting

title: Pedestrian Waterlogging & Electrical Hazard Precaution
guidance: Sustained rainfall leads to submerged curbs, open utility hazards, and potential electrical leakage around municipal transformer poles and streetlights.
precautions: Wear waterproof anti-skid footwear with ankle support
Avoid wading through opaque standing water of unknown depth
Stay strictly clear of downed utility wires, submerged electrical junctions, and metal lamp posts

title: Precipitation & Low-Traction Warning for Two-Wheeler Commute
guidance: High probability of rain creates reduced roadway friction, hydroplaning risks, and diminished visor visibility. Warn commuters of potential traffic delays and braking distance degradation.
precautions: Increase following distance to at least 4-5 seconds behind leading vehicles
Inspect tire tread depth and headlight illumination prior to departure
Check live transit and localized waterlogging alerts before leaving

title: Outdoor Picnic & Leisure Composite Comfort Index
guidance: Composite recreational comfort assessment evaluated across thermal moderation, atmospheric stability, cloud shelter, and precipitation risk. When metrics align within comfort tolerances, conditions are highly suitable for outdoor leisure and dining.
precautions: Set up picnic seating beneath natural canopy or portable gazebo
Keep perishable food items stored in insulated cold coolers
Have a secondary indoor contingency plan if localized convective showers develop

title: Optimal Weather Advisory for Outdoor Physical Training
guidance: Favorable, safe conditions for outdoor cardiovascular training, cycling, and general fitness activities with minimal environmental stress.
precautions: Maintain routine hydration
Standard baseline warm-up and cool-down protocols apply
